private_notes.observations: No rate cards, allocation outcomes, or competitor prices are available yet. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start at a moderate markup, then use subsequent rate cards and allocated hours to assess price sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: No prior rate cards or allocation data are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start at a moderate rate that balances margin against the risk of losing hours. Use subsequent rate cards and allocated hours to adjust.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, both panel firms charged $350; Arden & Cole received 845 hours and reported $126,696 in profit. One quarter does not establish how sensitive Meridian's allocation is to rate changes.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to test price sensitivity. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1, then adjust based on the observed response.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, both firms charged $350, and Birchwood Hale received 845 hours, earning approximately $126,696. There is no evidence yet of how Meridian reallocates hours when rates differ.
private_notes.plan: Keep the $350 rate as a stable benchmark rather than starting a price war. Use future rate cards and allocated hours to assess whether a higher rate would improve long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $350 to $375 while Birchwood Hale stayed at $350 coincided with a drop in allocated hours from 845 to 614 and lower quarterly profit. The allocation formula is unknown, so this does not establish an exact demand curve.
private_notes.plan: Test a rate below Birchwood Hale’s $350 to see whether increased hours outweigh the reduced margin. Compare the resulting profit and hours with Q1 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $350, allocated hours rose from 845 to 1,013 when Arden & Cole raised its rate from $350 to $375. The $350 rate produced about $152,000 in Q2 profit.
private_notes.plan: Keep $350 this quarter. The observed increase in hours suggests that raising our rate by $25 could reduce volume enough to outweigh the higher margin. Reassess after seeing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: With Birchwood Hale at $350 throughout, lowering our rate from $350 to $330 increased quarterly profit from $126,696 to $135,634. Raising it to $375 reduced profit to $107,519.
private_notes.plan: Test $318, near the estimated profit-maximizing rate based on the observed relationship between our rate and allocated hours. Reassess after seeing Q4 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $350, hours were 1,013 when Arden & Cole charged $375, but fell to 699 when it charged $330. Our relative price appears to affect allocation, though quarterly demand may also vary.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate modestly to match the latest competing rate. Assess whether the additional hours compensate for the lower margin, then update based on the Q4 allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q3 produced the highest profit ($135,634) at $330, when Birchwood Hale charged $350. Cutting our rate to $318 in Q4 did not increase our hours or profit, though Birchwood Hale also cut its rate to $330.
private_notes.plan: Return to $330 rather than continue cutting rates. Monitor whether Birchwood Hale holds at $330 and reassess the profit-versus-hours tradeoff next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Q4’s $330 rate yielded 794 hours and $103,263 profit, slightly below Q3’s $104,906 at $350. Arden & Cole has lowered its rate for two consecutive quarters, reaching $318.
private_notes.plan: Set $340 to recover some margin without moving too far above the competing rate. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q4 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $330, quarterly profit was $135,634 when Birchwood Hale charged $350 and $125,888 when it charged $340. Cutting to $318 yielded only $119,155; raising to $375 yielded $107,519.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $330. The observed gains in hours from a deeper discount have not offset the lower margin. Reassess if Birchwood Hale's rate or our allocated hours shift materially.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q5, profit rose to $110,997 from $103,263 at $330 in Q4, with nearly identical allocated hours. At $350 when the other firm charged $330, allocated hours and profit were lower than in Q5.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340 to preserve the Q5 margin and volume balance. Reassess after observing the next allocation and published rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $330 against Birchwood Hale’s $340, we earned $125,888 in both Q5 and Q6. The Q3–Q4 results suggest that a modestly lower rate could increase hours enough to improve profit, though the allocation formula is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test $315 this quarter. Compare the resulting hours and profit with the $330 baseline, accounting for any change in Birchwood Hale’s rate.

private_notes.observations: At $340 against Arden & Cole's $330, allocation and profit were identical in Q5 and Q6: 793 hours and $110,997. The observed $350 rate against a $330 competitor earned less profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold $340 while the competitor remains near $330; reassess if its rate or our allocation changes.

private_notes.observations: With Birchwood Hale at $340, our $315 rate earned $128,548 in Q7, versus $125,888 at $330 in Q5 and Q6. The extra hours more than offset the lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $315 and monitor both firms’ rates and our allocated hours. Reassess if Birchwood Hale changes its rate or allocation shifts materially.

private_notes.observations: At $340, our allocated hours fell from 793 when Arden & Cole charged $330 to 678 when it charged $315. The $330 rate previously earned about $103,000 in a quarter with Arden & Cole at $318.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate modestly to regain hours without initiating a steep price cut. Reassess after seeing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At Birchwood Hale’s current $330 rate, our $315 rate earned approximately $120,000 in each of Q4 and Q8. Higher rates have sometimes earned more, but those quarters also had a higher rival rate, making the comparison uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Keep our rate at $315 for Q9. Monitor allocated hours and the published rate card before considering another change; avoid cutting margin without evidence that additional hours would compensate.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole held at $315 in Q7–Q8. Cutting our rate from $340 to $330 increased allocated hours from 678 to 770 and quarterly profit from about $94,900 to $100,100.
private_notes.plan: Test a further modest reduction to $325 to improve our allocation while preserving margin. Reassess using next quarter's hours and published rate card; avoid a steep price cut.

private_notes.observations: At $315, allocated hours fell from 1,118 in Q7 to 999 in Q9 as Birchwood’s rate fell from $340 to $325. The resulting Q9 profit was $114,919. Earlier, $330 generated stronger profits when Birchwood charged $340–$350, but those comparisons may not hold at its current rate.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to preserve a modest price advantage while recovering $10 of margin per hour. Reassess after seeing the next allocation and rate card; avoid a larger increase until there is evidence it would improve profit.

private_notes.observations: At Arden & Cole’s $315 rate, reducing ours from $340 to $330 to $325 coincided with higher allocated hours and improved quarterly profit, though allocations may vary for other reasons.
private_notes.plan: Match the competing rate at $315 to test whether additional hours offset the narrower margin. Reassess profit and the next published rate card before cutting further.

private_notes.observations: At $325 against Birchwood Hale’s $315 in Q10, our profit fell to $102,269. Historically, rates near $315–$330 have produced stronger profits when we were priced below Birchwood Hale.
private_notes.plan: Set $315 to regain a competitive position without a steep margin cut. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $315 against Arden & Cole’s $325, we earned $114,919 last quarter. Recent higher rates generally produced less profit when Arden & Cole priced near or below us.
private_notes.plan: Hold $315 rather than raise the rate after a successful quarter. Reassess if the competitor’s rate or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood Hale matched our $315 rate in Q11. At $315, we received 916 hours and earned about $105,375; in Q10, charging $325 against Birchwood Hale's $315 yielded 818 hours and about $102,269.
private_notes.plan: Set a modest $5 discount to seek more hours without sacrificing much margin. Reassess profit and Birchwood Hale's rate next quarter rather than pursuing a steep price cut.

private_notes.observations: At $315, allocated hours were 999 and 916 in the last two quarters, producing profits of $114,919 and $105,375. Arden & Cole's latest rate was $315. Recent higher rates have not consistently generated higher profit.
private_notes.plan: Keep the $315 rate while monitoring Arden & Cole's rate and our allocated hours. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: Recent results suggest a $5 undercut of Birchwood Hale's $315 rate produced little profit improvement over matching it: Q12 profit was $106,273 at $310, versus $105,375 at $315 in Q11. Quarterly hours also vary independently of price.
private_notes.plan: Match Birchwood Hale's latest $315 rate to preserve margin without escalating a price-cutting cycle. Reassess allocation and profit after Q13.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole's rate fell to $310 in Q12. At our $315 rate, allocated hours fell from 916 to 874. Historically, rates between $315 and $325 have produced similar quarterly profits, around $100,000–$115,000.
private_notes.plan: Set $320 as a modest increase that may improve margin without sacrificing too many hours. Monitor the next allocation and rate card before making a larger change.

private_notes.observations: At $315 against Birchwood Hale’s $320 in Q13, we earned $110,179. Recent rate cuts have not consistently improved profit; $330 earned more when Birchwood Hale charged $340–$350.
private_notes.plan: Set $320 to test a modest margin increase while remaining close to Birchwood Hale’s latest rate. Review allocated hours and profit next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At a competing rate of $315, our profit was about $105,375 at $315, $104,028 at $320, and $102,269 at $325. The $320 increase did not improve profit over the comparable $315 quarter.
private_notes.plan: Return to $315 to recover hours while preserving a strong margin. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $320 against Birchwood Hale’s $315 in Q14, profit fell to $104,028. At $315 against its $320 in Q13, profit was $110,179. Recent results favor staying competitive rather than raising the rate.
private_notes.plan: Set $315 for Q15. Reassess hours, profit, and Birchwood Hale’s rate after the quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $315, recent quarterly profits have ranged from about $100,500 to $110,200, depending on Arden & Cole’s rate. Raising our rate to $320–$330 has not reliably improved profit, while $315 has generally secured more hours.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $315 to preserve a strong margin and competitive allocation. Reassess after the next rate card and hours allocation.

private_notes.observations: When Birchwood charged $315, our profit was about $105,375 at $315, $104,028 at $320, and $106,273 at $310. Lowering our rate modestly increased hours enough to offset the smaller margin.
private_notes.plan: Set $305 for Q16 based on the observed allocation response. Reassess profit and Birchwood’s published rate next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At a competitor rate of $315, our $315 rate yielded 916 hours and about $105,375 profit in both Q11 and Q15. Our $320–$330 rates against the same competitor rate produced lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $315 to balance margin and allocated hours. Reassess if the competitor's rate or our allocation changes materially.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood has held at $315 for the last two quarters. Against that rate, our observed profits were $105,375 at $315, $106,273 at $310, and $106,691 at $305.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $305 while Birchwood remains near $315; reassess if its rate or our allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $315, recent quarterly profit ranged from about $96,000 to $115,000, depending on Arden & Cole's rate. Its latest rate fell to $305, and our allocation dropped to 832 hours.
private_notes.plan: Hold $315 rather than react to one quarter of lower competitor pricing. Monitor whether Arden & Cole maintains $305 and whether our hours remain depressed before changing course.

private_notes.observations: With Birchwood at $315, our $305 rate produced about $106,691 in each of the last two quarters, slightly above the profits observed at our $310 and $315 rates against the same rival rate.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $305 while Birchwood remains near $315; reassess if its rate or our allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $315 against Arden & Cole’s $305, we received 832 hours in both Q16 and Q17, earning about $95,670 each quarter. Historical allocations suggest a modest rate cut may add hours, but the reduced margin is unlikely to improve profit materially.
private_notes.plan: Keep the $315 rate rather than initiate a price-cutting cycle. Reassess if Arden & Cole changes its rate or our allocated hours decline further.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood has held at $315 for eight of the last nine quarters. At that competing rate, our $305 yielded approximately $106,691 per quarter, slightly more than observed profits at $310, $315, or $320.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $305 while Birchwood stays near $315 and allocation remains stable. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole has held at $305 for three quarters, while our $315 rate has consistently produced about 832 hours and $95,670 profit per quarter. Earlier quarters at $315 were more profitable when Arden & Cole charged more.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $315 rather than initiate a price-cutting cycle for a modest and uncertain short-term gain. Reassess if Arden & Cole changes its rate or our hours decline.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood has held at $315 for four quarters. At our $305 rate, we received 1,016 hours and earned $106,691 each quarter, slightly more than at the other recently tested rates.
private_notes.plan: Keep $305 while Birchwood's rate and our allocation remain stable. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole has held its rate at $305 for four consecutive quarters. At our $315 rate, we received 832 hours and earned approximately $95,670 each quarter. Historical results suggest a rate cut would offer little certain profit improvement.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $315 to avoid a price-cutting cycle. Reassess if Arden & Cole changes its rate or our allocated hours fall.
